$comment: Page Watch vocabulary registry. Source of truth for user-facing status words. Decided in Chunk F1. CHANGELOG: v4 closed three gaps C1a surfaced. v5 closed the gaps the F1/F2/F3/C1 build report surfaced — Resolved had no legal entry, checkpoints had no vocabulary or evaluation rule, and two measuring systems shared one evidence slot. v6 added rules 18 and 19 from S1. v7 added rules 20 and 21 from R1, and extended rule 18 with the withhold-versus-fail distinction after a wrong ruling on F3. v8 added concepts.action.actor_note. v9 is v8's content with tightened prose on rules 18, 20 and 21 and this changelog — renumbered because a registry that changes its content without changing its number is the drift it exists to prevent, and two files numbered 8 already differed. v10 renames evidence_source.kitesurf's label from the codename Kitesurf to Rendered page, from S9: a name only the team could read was the one name that system had on screen, and S9's rule is that no term may appear as jargon alone. The key is unchanged — a data key is not copy.

work_state.description: Where one issue case is in its lifecycle. Exactly one at a time.

values.label: New
values.means: Detected and corroborated. Nobody has looked yet.

values.label: To do
values.means: Somebody said yes. Nobody has started.

values.label: Fixed
values.means: The change shipped. Evidence has not agreed yet.

values.label: Reopened
values.means: A check found the problem back. Needs a new decision.

values.label: Dismissed
values.means: Deliberately excluded. Off-ramp from Decide only, and it requires a reason.
values.absorbs: Native-element 'acknowledged' (nativeElements.ts) — a real finding that still counts, which the user has seen and chosen not to act on. That is dismissed + reason 'Intentional', which is in this value's reasons list above. Folded in S3 when native-element findings become issue cases.

queue.description: A filter over work_state. Named with a verb, because a queue is a job.

action.description: The verbs that move an issue between states. One lifecycle, no synonyms. Every legal move is here, whether a person or the system fires it — actor says which.
action.actor_note: actor is a PERMISSION SET, not an identity: it says which classes of caller may fire this transition. It is not the record of who did. Those are two meanings for one word, which rule 4 forbids — so the runtime records the identity separately (by: "checkpoint", by: a user id) and validates that identity's CLASS against this list. 'checkpoint' is a system caller; a user id is a person caller. Validation is on the class, never on the string, which is why a richer identity string is legal and an unpermitted class is not. Added in v9 after W1 found applyAction recording actor without validating it: 'resolve is system-only' held because the evaluator was its only caller, not because anything enforced it — a stated rule with no mechanism, which is the gap rule 14 exists to name.

values.label: Mark fixed
values.note: Schedules the three checkpoints. See the checkpoint concept for what reads them.

values.label: Resolve
values.note: Added in v5. Nobody presses this — no button carries the label. The 30-day checkpoint fires it when every checkpoint that produced a reading agreed. Before v5 Resolved had no legal entry, which rule 14 now names as the same bug as a state with no legal exit. History reads 'Resolved — the 30-day check agreed', never 'auto-resolved'.

values.label: Reopen
values.note: From fixed the system fires it: a 2, 7, or 30-day checkpoint disagreed, so the change did not hold. From resolved it came back later. From dismissed a person changed their mind. All three land in Decide. Legal since v4 — an implementer working from v2 or v3 will find this transition missing and should not add it locally.

checkpoint.description: One scheduled re-measurement of a fixed issue: 2, 7 and 30 days after Mark fixed. Three per issue, drawn as the three dots on the case. Not a lifecycle state — the issue stays Fixed while they run. Added in v5, because mark_fixed scheduled these and nothing named or read them.

values.label: Scheduled
values.means: Due in the future. Nothing has been measured yet.

values.label: Agreed
values.means: The re-measurement no longer finds the problem.

values.label: Disagreed
values.means: The re-measurement still finds the problem.

values.label: Unavailable
values.means: No reading could be taken — the page did not answer, or the collector had no data for the window. Neither agreement nor disagreement. Same condition as agent_result.unavailable on a different object, which rule 4 allows.

evaluation: A checkpoint that disagrees fires reopen at once. Remaining checkpoints are cancelled: the case is back in Decide, and the next mark_fixed schedules a fresh set of three.
Unavailable neither advances nor reopens. Retry once at +24h, then record Unavailable and carry on to the next checkpoint.
The 30-day checkpoint fires resolve when every checkpoint that produced a reading agreed. Unavailable readings are skipped, not counted against.
Three unavailable readings do not resolve. The case stays Fixed and says no check could be taken; the user may Reopen it or leave it in Watch.
The 2 and 7-day checkpoints never resolve on their own. Rule 5 says Resolved means the evidence agreed and held, and holding takes the full 30 days.
checkpoint.note: Passed and Failed belong to agent_result, on a check. A checkpoint is not a check: it asks whether an earlier conclusion still holds, so it agrees or disagrees with that conclusion. Confirmed belongs to confidence.

evidence_source.description: Who took a reading in the evidence ledger. One entry per system, never a blend — the ledger exists so that two systems disagreeing is visible rather than averaged away.

values.label: Agent readiness checks
values.means: Page Watch's own HTTP and markup checks. From v5 this slot carries only Page Watch's reading.

values.label: Rendered page
values.means: The published page opened in a real browser, recorded as it actually rendered. v10 renames the label: the key stays, because a data key is not copy, but the codename was the only name a reader ever saw for this system and a codename explains nothing.

evidence_source.note: v5 gives Ora its own slot. One slot for two systems meant confidenceFrom counted them as a single voice, so a disagreement between Page Watch and Ora could never surface — the exact failure the ledger was built to catch. is-agentic is removed: it had no producer, and an empty slot reads to the user as a reading that found nothing (rule 15).

trend.description: Direction of the score line. Never a statement about health.

health.description: How the page is doing right now, independent of direction.

confidence.description: How much the evidence supports the diagnosis. Any disagreement between sources lands on unclear — a majority does not carry the conclusion.

actionability.description: What the customer can do about this case. Decides whether Accept is offered at all.

values.label: Direct fix
values.means: There is a documented change the customer can make.

values.label: Workaround
values.means: No direct fix, but there is a documented way around it.

values.label: Platform
values.means: Webflow owns this one. Nothing for the customer to do; the case is shown so the reading is not hidden.

values.label: No action available
values.means: No documented remediation exists yet. Accept is not offered.

actionability.note: Migration from CustomerActionability: none maps to platform (it was only written where the platform owns the audit on a Webflow page), review maps to none (no documented remediation, so there is nothing to accept — and that correctly blocks Accept). Rule 17: a none case must say in one sentence why there is no action, or it reads as a broken card.

agent_result.description: Outcome of one agent-readiness check. Unchanged from the audit.

agent_verdict.description: One product conclusion for agent access on an origin. Never a provider score stack.

applicability.description: Whether a check or a detected element footprint counts toward this site's results. Not a lifecycle: it says whether something applies, not how far along it is. Applies to agent checks, check groups, and native-element findings alike.

values.label: Excluded
values.means: Deliberately not counted, because it does not apply to this site.

applicability.note: An excluded check still shows its last reading, greyed, with the reason. Excluding is not deleting — the audit is explicit that hiding evidence without saying why is how the agent tab lost trust. NOTE: the two native-element dispositions belong to DIFFERENT concepts, which is why no single word covered both. suppressed (skips hotspots, stops counting) is applicability → excluded. acknowledged (still counts, tallied separately, you have seen it) is lifecycle → dismissed with reason "Intentional". Do not invent a third concept for it.

rules: Filters and queues are verbs. Statuses are conditions. Show all is the unfiltered view, not a queue.
A state names the issue's situation now, in the plainest word that is true.
Progress inside a state is shown as detail, never as another state.

No word carries two different meanings. The same word MAY label the same condition on different objects — health.needs_work and agent_verdict.needs_work are both 'this is not good enough yet', on a page and on an origin, and should stay identical.
Where two words could read as synonyms, say the difference in the copy: Fixed means waiting on evidence, Resolved means evidence agreed.
Prefer the word a non-technical reader would use: fixed over implemented, no change over stable, reopened over returned.
Reuse a colour before inventing one. Seven states, five tones.
A status chip is 12px, weight 600, and never smaller than 12px. Nothing carrying meaning renders below 12px — the earlier 11px floor contradicted F3 and is withdrawn.
A banned_as_label term is only banned in that concept's label position. Only banned_global is enforced as prose.
Applicability is not lifecycle. If a control decides whether something counts, it is Exclude/Include — never a state.

Before adding a concept, check whether an existing one already means it. Two words for one idea is the failure this registry exists to prevent; a new concept for a state an existing one covers is the same failure wearing different clothes.
A state with no legal exit is a bug in this file, not a case for inventing a transition. If an implementer finds one, the registry is wrong.

A token is named for its role. A fill value used as ink, or a hairline value used as type, is a bug even though the token resolves — check contrast at the size and surface it is actually used at, not the one it was designed for.

A state with no legal entry is the same bug as a state with no legal exit. Every state needs a way in and a way out, and the transition that provides it lives here, not in an implementer's local patch.
An evidence slot with no producer is not a slot. Define it when something writes to it: an empty slot reads to the user as a reading that found nothing.
A transition the system fires still writes history in the words the user reads. 'Resolved — the 30-day check agreed', never 'auto_resolved'.
When a case offers no action, it says why in one sentence. An action-less card with no explanation reads as a broken product, not as an honest one.

An absent measurement is not a small measurement. A finding with no reading is never folded, filtered or ranked as though its value were zero — it sorts last within its group and its row says 'not measured', never 0. Same principle as checkpoint.unavailable: no reading is neither good news nor bad. The response to absence is to WITHHOLD the claim, not to fail — a conclusion that depends on a reading nobody took is simply not stated, while a broken invariant, a shape that should have been impossible, fails loudly and names what was malformed. Confusing the two trades a false claim for a crashed screen. And withholding good news must never swallow bad news: a claim withheld for want of data still reports every drop it did measure.

A number shown for a group is the same statistic as the number shown for one member: the worst observed reading, never a sum. Adding measurements across findings invents a figure no run produced, and a group total that cannot be reconciled with the rows beneath it is worse than no total.

A fact stated twice is a defect waiting, so state it once. Where a second statement is genuinely unavoidable — a pre-paint script that cannot import, a type that must not reach a provider module — the second copy carries a test that executes or type-checks the two against each other. A comment asking the next editor to keep them in step is not a mechanism; every drift found in R1 had exactly such a comment and nothing else.

A test asserts the decision, not the code. Asserting a literal that vocabulary.json also names is asserting a mirror against a mirror: it proves two copies agree, never that either is right. Assert against the registry, or against the other half of the decision, so the test fails the moment the halves disagree.

banned_global.$comment: Hard-gated: these must not appear in user-facing copy anywhere in src/. This is the list the eslint rule enforces. A concept's banned_as_label list is narrower — it means 'not a valid label for THIS concept', not 'never write this word'.

allowlist.$comment: Pre-existing violations in files C1a does not own. Each entry names the chunk that clears it. The list may only shrink. webflow-connection.tsx was cleared in C1a and removed in v5 — the rename it covered is done and the entry was dead. pages/[id]/page.tsx was cleared in S3 and removed: the tabs it named are gone and the native-element dispositions are now the applicability and work_state concepts below. watchlist/page.tsx was cleared in S8 and removed: the settings mode that carried the Ignore/Suppress copy moved to /settings and became the applicability concept below, and the watchlist itself never used those words. agent-access.tsx was cleared in S4 and removed: the two route references were the Tasks button, which now names the Fix queue. guide.ts was cleared in S9 and removed: the glossary is deleted, and the retired-term definitions it carried went with the file rather than moving anywhere.
allowlist.src/components/bits.tsx: F2 — Verifying/Returned belong to the lifecycles F2 deletes
allowlist.src/components/store.tsx: S2 — route references to the retired destinations
